name: SAP Ariba
description: SAP Ariba and SAP Business Network cover procurement, sourcing, suppliers, contracts, catalogs, orders, invoices, payments, and trading-partner collaboration. API availability depends on the licensed solution, customer realm or network identifier, region, and SAP approval.
agentUseSummary: SAP Ariba cannot yet be connected through Relay. The provider offers separate solution-specific APIs rather than one Ariba account API, and production access requires a licensed organization, administrator-requested approval for a particular API and realm, an application key, and OAuth credentials. Relay has no approved solution, API, realm, document, supplier, transaction, or financial-authority contract.

blocked.label: Connect SAP Ariba
blocked.description: A licensed organization, selected API and solution, customer realm or network identifier, organization-admin request, SAP production approval, application key, and OAuth identity are required.

blocked.label: Read spend and supplier data
blocked.description: Suppliers, questionnaires, bids, sourcing events, contracts, catalogs, orders, receipts, service sheets, invoices, payments, and other procurement data remain unavailable.

blocked.label: Change procurement records
blocked.description: Creating, updating, submitting, approving, rejecting, awarding, ordering, confirming, shipping, receiving, invoicing, paying, or otherwise changing procurement documents is blocked.

blocked.label: Administer or bulk-process Ariba
blocked.description: Applications, realms, users, suppliers, catalogs, templates, custom forms, RPA bots, imports, exports, bulk extraction, and configuration are blocked.

blocked.label: Use raw or private interfaces
blocked.description: Arbitrary APIs, cXML, private endpoints, browser automation, credential capture, unapproved applications, and privilege probing are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No SAP Ariba action is enabled without one exact licensed solution, API, realm, document set, business purpose, role, and procurement-control contract.

runtimeSupport.description: No SAP Ariba tools are mounted before solution, realm, data, document, role, and procurement-control boundaries are approved.
No SAP Ariba tools are mounted before solution, realm, data, document, role, and procurement-control boundaries are approved.

providerSetup.blocker: SAP Ariba is a family of licensed spend-management and Business Network solutions with separate APIs, prerequisites, regions, realms, network identifiers, and document models. SAP requires a customer organization, administrator and developer accounts, an application for selected APIs, one application per realm/API combination in most cases, organization-admin access requests, and SAP production approval before issuing an OAuth client ID. Calls require both an application key and OAuth token. Some third-party access also requires partner participation and written customer consent. A generic connector would obscure which supplier, sourcing, contract, order, invoice, payment, or administrative authority was granted.
providerSetup.nextAction: Product, procurement, finance, accounts-payable, legal, privacy, security, audit, and customer owners must select one licensed Ariba solution, API, realm or network identifier, region, business outcome, documents, fields, counterparties, roles, operations, approvals, monetary limits, segregation-of-duties controls, retention, audit, reconciliation, and incident duties. The customer organization administrator must then request the required production API access and obtain any SAP or partner approval. Only after that may Relay implement pinned typed wrappers with strict fields, bounds, approvals for every mutation, idempotency, reconciliation, audit, and post-disable denial.

evidence.supports: SAP requires licensed Ariba or Business Network solutions, regional administrator access, and solution-specific API prerequisites.
Applications select specific APIs, generally map one application to each realm/API combination, and require organization-admin requests plus SAP production approval.
Production access is requested for a particular API, solution, procurement or sourcing realm, Business Network identifier, or customer ID and cannot be used until approved.
Every API request requires both the application's API key and an OAuth token; optional mutual authentication is available.
One representative API is tied to specific supplier solutions, sites, SAP approval, and third-party partner and written-consent requirements.
